spans.s:
dvyaṇuka
(‘of two atoms’)
------------------------------------------
Creation of this world is a topic that is invariably discussed in the darśanas or systems of इन्दिअन् फिलोसोफ्य्. The वैशेषिक दर्शन of कणाद accepts paramāṇus or atoms of earth, water, fire and air as the four fundamental substances from which this physical universe evolves.
Impelled by the कर्म of the unredeemed jīvas or individual souls, at the beginning of the च्रेअतिओन्, two paramāṇus are united forming a ‘dvyaṇuka’. Three such dvyaṇukas join together making a ‘tryaṇuka’. This process goes on till the entire physical world is finally created. (vide Brahmasūtras

and शङ्कर’s commentary on the same.)
See also VAIŚEṢIKA-DARŚANA.
